input: "Criticism is welcome. I'm not promising to agree with it before I see the line, but I'd like to know." I hand Caelindra the pages and move my tea clear so she has room to point without risking the manuscript. Then I tell Rashid, "You're welcome to send Nahla a copy if you think she'd enjoy it. She can tell me what I got wrong about the goat."
output:
Caelindra draws the pages toward her, keeping her cup at a distance fit for dangerous machinery. She reads the final paragraph again, then places one immaculate fingernail beneath a sentence.

“‘Thus pride charged a dearer toll than any bridgekeeper.’ This line.” Her violet eyes lift to yours. “The sign has already said it more gracefully. Explaining afterward suggests you do not trust the reader to notice.”

“I noticed,” Thessaly says.

Ashara leans across the chair back. “Cut it.”

Caelindra’s ears angle sharply. “I was addressing the author.”

“And I am agreeing with you. Try to endure it.”

She returns the pages unmarked. “Keep it if you disagree. It is at least your own mistake to make.”

Rashid, meanwhile, looks genuinely pleased by the offer. “Nahla will consider this serious correspondence. Expect green ink, demands for the goat’s name, and perhaps a diagram correcting its behavior.” He closes the pastry box. “I’ll copy it myself. If one of our secretaries sees it, they’ll turn the whole thing into an improving fable about fiscal responsibility.”

Seraphel nods solemnly.

“A child, green ink, a goat well fed—  
You’ll write twelve sequels ere she’s through.”

The clock begins its warning chime. On the second note, Aldric appears in the doorway already immaculate in white and gold.

“The reception begins in eleven minutes.”

“We know,” says Ashara.

“You are wearing training trousers.”

“They are formal training trousers.”

Aldric looks briefly toward the ceiling, as if requesting strength from a Divine Light overburdened by tailoring. “Garvey, dark formal coat, signet, no sash. The chancellor is particular.”

Chairs empty in a rush of cups and folded napkins. Rashid leaves the last lemon pastry beside your manuscript before following Ashara upstairs. The disputed sentence waits beneath Caelindra’s faint thumbnail mark.
